sections.title: Income tax: individuals

source.title: TF1 – Individual Income Tax Return (taxation year ending 31 March), with the tax table and low income rebate calculation

sections.basis: taxable income of an individual for the taxation year ending 31 March
sections.note: From the tax table on the TF1 individual return (the rate table in Part B of Schedule 1 of the Income Tax Act is not in the reprint's text layer): tax of $1,000 on $10,000 and $3,000 on $20,000, then 30 cents per dollar above $20,000. Rebates (personal, low income, dependants, church donations) reduce the tax (separate rows). The source gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026-27 tax year (1 April 2026).

rows.label: Income tax: personal rebate
rows.note: rebate claimed by each individual taxpayer on the TF1 return. The source gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026-27 tax year (1 April 2026).

source.title: TF1 – Individual Income Tax Return (taxation year ending 31 March), with the tax table and low income rebate calculation

rows.label: Income tax: low income rebate (maximum)
rows.note: maximum low income rebate for assessable income under $20,000 (full amount below $10,000; reduced by 10 cents per dollar above $10,000, nil at $20,000); not for absentees, companies or the self-employed. The source gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026-27 tax year (1 April 2026).

source.title: TF1 – Individual Income Tax Return (taxation year ending 31 March), with the tax table and low income rebate calculation

rows.label: Income tax: low income rebate abatement (per dollar above $10,000)
rows.note: assessable income above $10,000 (reduces the $1,000 low income rebate to nil at $20,000). The source gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026-27 tax year (1 April 2026).

source.title: TF1 – Individual Income Tax Return (taxation year ending 31 March), with the tax table and low income rebate calculation

rows.label: Income tax: low income rebate for private-sector employees (maximum)
rows.note: maximum low income rebate for full-time employees (20 hours or more a week for at least 40 weeks) earning under $20,000 whose primary employment is outside the Niue Public Service and statutory bodies. The source gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026-27 tax year (1 April 2026).

source.title: TF1 – Individual Income Tax Return (taxation year ending 31 March), with the tax table and low income rebate calculation

rows.label: Income tax: dependent relative rebate (per dependant)
rows.note: each dependent relative. The source gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026-27 tax year (1 April 2026).

source.title: TF1 – Individual Income Tax Return (taxation year ending 31 March), with the tax table and low income rebate calculation

rows.label: Income tax: church donations rebate (20 cents a dollar, up to $100)
rows.note: church donations (rebate of 20 cents per dollar donated, receipts attached). The source gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026-27 tax year (1 April 2026).

source.title: TF1 – Individual Income Tax Return (taxation year ending 31 March), with the tax table and low income rebate calculation

rows.label: Income tax: life insurance and superannuation exemption (up to $800)
rows.note: life insurance and superannuation for the taxpayer, spouse and children (special exemption from assessable income). The source gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026-27 tax year (1 April 2026).

source.title: TF1 – Individual Income Tax Return (taxation year ending 31 March), with the tax table and low income rebate calculation

rows.label: Income tax: primary produce exemption (first $5,000)
rows.note: income from the production of primary produce during the tax year (first $5,000 exempt). The source gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026-27 tax year (1 April 2026).

source.title: TF1 – Individual Income Tax Return (taxation year ending 31 March), with the tax table and low income rebate calculation
TF1 – Individual Income Tax Return (taxation year ending 31 March), with the tax table and low income rebate calculation

rows.label: PAYE: employer deductions and returns
rows.value: Employers deduct PAYE from weekly or fortnightly pay and deposit it to Treasury through the Tax Administration Office to the employee's credit, with the TF3 monthly return by the 20th and the TF4 annual summary by 20 April; individuals file the TF1 return by 31 August and assessed tax is due by 31 January
rows.note: The source gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026-27 tax year (1 April 2026).

source.title: Niue Tax Office: due dates, forms, guides (income tax, business licences, business tax obligations) and legislation

rows.label: PAYE: withholding on secondary employment (tax code SEC)
rows.note: salary or wages from an employment other than the employee's primary employment (tax code SEC). The source gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026-27 tax year (1 April 2026).

rows.label: Income tax: companies
rows.note: taxable income derived by a company in Niue (non-resident companies declare income derived in Niue only). The source gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026-27 tax year (1 April 2026).

source.title: Income Tax Act 1961 (Niue Legislation Act 2019 reprint)
Income Tax Act 1961 (Niue Legislation Act 2019 reprint)

rows.label: Niue Consumption Tax registration threshold
rows.note: taxable supplies made or expected in a 12-month period (associates' supplies may be counted); businesses with gross revenue over $75,000. The source gives no separate start date for this figure; stored from the start of the 2026-27 tax year (1 April 2026).

source.title: Niue Consumption Tax Act 2009

rows.label: Niue Consumption Tax (NCT) standard rate
rows.note: taxable supplies by taxable persons and taxable imports.

source.title: Niue Consumption Tax Act 2009

rows.label: NCT exemptions
rows.value: Exempt: financial services, precious metal, donated goods and services supplied by non-profit bodies, sales and long-term leases of residential premises (other than new premises) and residential leases of 2 months or more
